newsitem.title: USA: U.S. concerned by political 'crisis' in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. concerned by political 'crisis' in Belarus.

text.p: The United States is concerned by a political crisis in Belarus in which President Alexander Lukashenko has apparently acted outside the country's constitution, the State Department said on Monday.
"The United States believes that it's a crisis that's causing, in fact, some damage in the political system, the political process," State Department spokesman Glyn Davies told reporters.
Lukashenko has been trying to change the constitution to introduce presidential rule in the former Soviet republic, and has scheduled a referendum for Sunday aimed at boosting his powers.
"There does not appear, in our view, to be any legal basis in the Belarus constitution for the action that President Lukashenko has been taking," Davies said.

"We are concerned, and that's why we've gone so far as to describe it as really a crisis that's occurring," Davies added, and urged Lukashenko and parliament to work together within the context of the existing constitution.
After a weekend of violent demonstrations in the Belarussian capital of Minsk, members of parliament said on Monday they had started impeachment moves against Lukashenko.

Lukashenko's top aide, Vladimir Zametalin, told Reuters the 42-year-old president could stop parliament from impeaching him even if the constitutional court approved such a decision. Asked if Lukashenko might dissolve parliament and the constitutional court, Zametalin said: "It's entirely possible. The president has many options."
